items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Herb Fleming on trombone, Cordic Wallace, bass... were the brass section.

ctx.x: Timmie was in the know as to what was happening in the jazz w world and knew the onwers of most of the clubs uptown and downtown So we talked about the band I should lead for a few days and then started to put the idea in action. Harry White, an ex-Cab Calloway trombonist, known as "Father" White, was also known as a fine arranger, but he had become an alchoholic victim, and was not in demand at the time. He started hanging out in Timmie's record shop also, and when we had worked out the details of my orchestra,…

We contacted a pianist named General Morgan and his first name really was General. He was a fine pianist. Arthur Herbert, who was an Ex-Coleman Hawkins drummer, Franz Jackson, a tenor man and Herb Fleming on trombone are the only known members of the orchestra that I can remember. "Father" White was living in a back room of the record shop and Timmie was feeding him and also gave him a little drinking money. The shop wasn't doing too well, so not much money was coming in, and we musicians weren't working, so we…

But things were going along nicely at the rehersals and one day, I think that Timmie or Inez hit the numbers for five cents and decided to have a little party for the band. Timmie had been speaking about a famous dish he used to cook called Danish meat balls, or fish balls, and he cooked some for the party. They were made with fish and mixed with mashed potatoes and served with a white sauce, and they were very tasty, to my surprise.

items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We made the rounds of different clubs, were invited to parties and dinners, including one that Herb Flemming prepared for us in his Bronx home.

ctx.x: We arrived in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, the next day. Our cousin Andre Hoffmann and his wife Denise met us and we drove to Sunbury where we spent the night and the next day, visiting the country. Left Sunbury via Harrisburg for New York which was a three hour trip with the train and had the same suite in the Hotel Schluyler that we occupied before going to Cincinnati. George, again, didn't want us to pay anything. We met his mother, Ismay, and we invited her to come to Europe for the summer. Lily offered her to…

We made the rounds of different clubs, were invited to parties and dinners, including one that Herb Flemming prepared for us in his Bronx home. We also caught Ben Webster on his opening night at the Village Vanguard. Ben had a fine trio backing him, but the only musician I can remember was Philly Jo Jones whom I had never met before. Later that night, Tony Scott came in and blew some baritone sax and had a gone jam session with Ben who was playing his can-off that night.

Saturday nights there was always a session at Central Plaza on East 3rd street which was run by Jack Crystal who at one time managed the sessions for Milt Gabler at Jimmie Rhyan on 52nd street. Jack was a real friend to all jazz musicians regardless of race or religion and his sessions were often a big help to many of the fellows that played them.
